title: Every roadmap writer is held to the note cap at commit, not only triage
why: Finding, Oct 27 (triage 8): other threads pushed notes over 250 words five times in one hour, and each blocked triage's next commit until triage trimmed someone else's note.
note: Today only triage gates its commits on build.py's upkeep line; other threads append to notes and push. Built and reviewed (2 Opus rounds), branch c138-roadmap-precommit head 4c5b0b3, not yet on roadmap; the orchestrator lands it: roadmap/hooks/pre-commit runs build.py --check-staged and refuses a commit that adds or grows an open step's note past 250 words; setup is `git config core.hooksPath roadmap/hooks` once per clone; 32 tests green (red on a synthetic note, since no c122 note ever passed 250). Known: a merge or cherry-pick of a --no-verify commit is unchecked. Was: a pre-commit hook on the roadmap branch (installed by a one-line setup the branch CLAUDE.md names) runs build.py and refuses a commit that leaves a note over 250 words, naming the note; red first on today's c122 append. Needs no answer. Port: no; the roadmap branch is claude-settings' own. Placed ahead of c107 (triage, Oct 27): it costs triage a trim on nearly every write.
